newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bourse extends strong run.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bourse extends strong run.

text.p: Nigerian shares surged further on Thursday it its current bull run, fuelled by frenzied buying.
The all-share index shot to 7,675.89 from 7,617.87 on Wednesday.
Activities were mostly in blue chips in the banking, manufacturing and petroleum marketing sectors.
"Investors are pumping more cash into shares from the low-yielding money markets where interests rates have fallen," one dealer said.
Most food/beverages stocks were higher on growing demand but Nigerian Bottling Company attracted the strongest bid, rising more than three percent or 1.00 naira to 43.00 naira.
Cadbury closed at 32.60 naira, up 55 kobo while Nestle finished at 60.75 naira, up 15 kobo.
Brewers ended mixed as Nigerian Breweries rose 50 kobo to 15.20 naira while Guinness fell to 7.10 naira, down 10 kobo.
The healthcare sector was also mixed as Smithkline Beecham and Evans, formerly Glaxo dropped 30 kobo and 3 kobo, respectively, to 7.00 naira and 4.85 naira.
Profit taking accounted for the Beecham drop while surplus shares depressed Evans, analysts said.
First Bank led its sector, adding 50 kobo to end at 13.85 naira. UBA and Union Bank each rose by 30 kobo to 10.20 naira and 12.00 naira, respectively.
Conglomerates also ended higher except for the tumbling PZ which closed 70 kobo down at 23.60 naira.
Lever Brothers rose to 21.10 naira while UAC finished 20 kobo up at 11.00 naira.
Oil marketers strengthened in undiminished demand. Unipetrol advanced to 72.50 naira, followed by Total which closed at 69.50 naira, up 20 kobo.
Traders said investors were also buying cheaper stocks in the industrial/domestic sector as well as insurance companies, causing their prices to also appreciate.
Beneficiaries included Industrial Gases and Vitafoam, 5 kobo gainers at 14.25 naira and 4.15 naira respectively while Royal Exchange Assurance rose 10 kobo to 3.40 naira.
